elements.element: Customer owns Deliverables and work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: §7(a) retains the default rule that "If not specified, Materials will be considered Type II Materials", and §7(c) leaves "all right, title, and interest (including ownership of copyright)" in Type II Materials with IBM. Only the sub-set designated Type I vests in Customer, so Customer does not own deliverables generally.

elements.element: Vendor assigns the Deliverables and work product to Customer.
elements.evidence: No assignment language anywhere in the rendered §7; Type I ownership vests by description only and Type II is expressly IBM-owned. The redline does not add an assignment of deliverables.

elements.element: Vendor retains its pre-existing intellectual property.
elements.evidence: §7(c) (unchanged in the operative direction): "Type II Materials are those, created during the Service performance period or otherwise (such as those that preexist the Service), in which IBM or third parties have all right, title, and interest (including ownership of copyright)."

elements.element: Customer's licence to Vendor IP embedded in Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: Redlined §7(c): "IBM grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, nonexclusive, worldwide, royalty-free license..." — Type II Materials are the IBM-owned IP delivered to Customer.

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: Redlined §7(c) retains "irrevocable" in the Type II grant.

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: Redlined §7(c) substitutes "royalty-free" for the original "paid-up" in the Type II grant.

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: The rendered text contains no affirmative statement that Customer owns or retains all rights in Content, Customer Components or other Customer data; the new §14.18 sentence only limits IBM's licence scope ("IBM's license in Content, Customer Components, and any other data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer is limited to processing such data solely to provide the Services"). To reach the preferred level, add an express "Customer retains all right, title and interest in Customer Data" sentence.

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: Redlined §14.18 deletes the "collective business activities... promotions, and for marketing research" grant and states contact information is stored and used "solely to provide the Services", plus the catch-all limiting IBM's licence in "Content, Customer Components, and any other data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer" to processing "solely to provide the Services".

elements.element: The parties do not jointly own intellectual property.
elements.evidence: §7 creates a binary Type I (Customer-owned) / Type II (IBM- or third-party-owned) architecture with no joint-ownership language; the redline does not introduce any.

elements.element: Vendor may retain ownership of generic tools and know-how.
elements.evidence: Already met and left undisturbed: §7(c) "Type II Materials are those, created during the Service performance period or otherwise (such as those that preexist the Service), in which IBM or third parties have all right, title, and interest (including ownership of copyright)."

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: Redlined §7(c): "IBM grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, nonexclusive, worldwide, royalty-free license..." — the word "perpetual" is newly inserted and appears in operative text, not merely the comment.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: "perpetual, irrevocable, nonexclusive, worldwide, royalty-free license" in redlined §7(c).

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is worldwide.
elements.evidence: "worldwide" retained in the redlined §7(c) grant, and the conflicting "within Customer's Enterprise only" restriction is deleted so the worldwide scope is no longer contradicted.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: Redlined §7(c) grants a "royalty-free" licence (replacing "paid-up"), matching the checklist term.

elements.element: Customer may use and modify Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: Redlined §7(c): licence "to use, execute, modify, reproduce, display, perform, distribute, and sublicense copies of Type II Materials for Customer's business purposes" — "modify" and the business-purpose scope are new.

elements.element: Customer may sublicense Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: "and sublicense copies of Type II Materials for Customer's business purposes" in redlined §7(c); the Enterprise-only limitation that would have defeated sublicensing is removed.

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: Redlined §14.18 removes the standing right to use contact data "anywhere they do business" and to pass it to "contractors, Business Partners, and assignees ... for promotions, and for marketing research", and substitutes "solely to provide the Services" plus a catch-all limiting IBM's licence in Content, Customer Components and any other Customer data to processing solely to provide the Services.

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete in operative language: §7(c) now reads perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, with use/modify/sublicense for Customer's business purposes, and §14.18 confines IBM's rights in Customer data to processing solely to provide the Services. IBM's ownership of Type II (generic/pre-existing) Materials is untouched.

Preferred level is not reached on two elements: there is no Vendor assignment of deliverables (Type II remains IBM-owned and is the default category under §7(a)), and there is no affirmative "Customer retains all rights in Customer Data" sentence. To upgrade, add an assignment of Materials created for Customer and an express Customer Data ownership statement.

Edits are confined to the two operative sentences that block the fallback. Deleting "within Customer's Enterprise only" is necessary because it directly contradicts the new worldwide/sublicense grant, and deleting the §14.18 "collective business activities ... promotions ... marketing research" sentence is necessary because it is the standing independent-exploitation right the data element must remove. Substituting "royalty-free" for "paid-up" is checklist wording, not a substantive loss; no survival tails, expense language or extraneous procedures were added.

Intent preserved: Type I ownership and the §7(b) licence-back to IBM, the §12.1 Base Components platform licence, the data-protection instructions sentence and the "contact information is not personal information processed on your behalf" sentence all survive intact and unamended.

Drafting point to tighten (not a defect that fails the checklist): the new §14.18 catch-all reaches "any other data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer", which could be read against the retained broad §7(b) licence in Customer-owned Type I Materials. Consider adding "Except as set out in Section 7," to the new sentence to remove any argument of inconsistency.

Classification as a deviation is correct: the pre-redline Type II licence was Enterprise-only with no modification, sublicensing or perpetual term, and §14.18 permitted marketing and Business Partner exploitation of Customer contact data — both material failures of the fallback, not minor sub-elements.
